- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.33) periods, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with historical mean reversion toward prior 10-day average.
- If forecast is below true outcome by >1.5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion bias” correction: add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% in first 5 days, assume momentum and apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 3 days.
- When sentiment swings from high to low, model often fails to adjust; apply “sentiment lag” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 2–3 days.
